data.title: Levocetirizine
data.summary: Antihistamines · Second-generation H1 antihistamine — active R-enantiomer of cetirizine
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** Second-generation H1 antihistamine — active R-enantiomer of cetirizine

## Mechanism of action
- Selective peripheral H1 inverse agonist; twice the receptor affinity of cetirizine

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic urticaria, allergic rhinitis, pruritus

## Dose & formulations
- 5 mg once daily in the evening (updosing up to 20 mg in urticaria); children 6–11 years 2.5 mg; 2–6 years 1.25 mg twice daily
- Halve or space doses in renal impairment

## Adverse effects
- Mild sedation (similar to cetirizine), dry mouth, fatigue

## Contraindications
- End-stage renal disease; children under 6 months

## Drug interactions
- Alcohol, CNS depressants

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data — cetirizine/loratadine preferred.

## Viva points
- 5 mg levocetirizine = 10 mg cetirizine; renal dose adjustment

_Sources: Khopkar (Second generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
